candidates.exact_span: The permittee must report total or total recoverable metal concentrations for compliance purpose. Because State WQS for aluminum and copper were dissolved-based criteria, the linear partition coefficient for copper to convert dissolved copper concentration to total concentration is used to calculate the maximum daily effluent limitation. However, because a partition coefficient for aluminum is not available, the effluent limitation for total aluminum is based on the dissolved criteria.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Different readings of whether limits and reported values are total/recoverable versus dissolved, and whether partition-coefficient conversion applies to aluminum versus copper, would change which numeric limit is compared to each measurement.

candidates.exact_span: The permit proposes to continue to include monitoring for hardness (CaCO3) for later RP analysis.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether hardness monitoring is an applicable ongoing requirement versus preparatory RP analysis affects whether monitoring was required during Federal FY2025.

candidates.exact_span: Aluminum did show RP, however because the prescribed daily and 30 day average limit concentration (3.2 mg/l) is less stringent than the limit in the previous permit, the previous limit will be maintained at the request of NMED and to comply with antibacksliding requirements.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether the operative aluminum limit is the newly calculated 3.2 mg/l or the antibacksliding-maintained previous limit changes which numeric standard is used for exceedance determinations.

candidates.exact_span: Permit limit of 0.75 mg/l daily max was previously established for aluminum based on water quality standards. It is proposed that the permit limit of 0.75 mg/l be applied to the 30 day average.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Applying a value established as a daily maximum to a 30-day average changes which limit type governs comparison and could alter whether reported daily versus average measurements exceed the applicable limit.

candidates.exact_span: Because aluminum exhibited RP, daily and 30 day loadings of 0.78 lbs/day will be established in the draft permit.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether enforceable limits include mass-loading caps of 0.78 lbs/day in addition to concentration limits affects which numeric discharge limits apply to loading-based measurements.

candidates.exact_span: Copper did not show RP, however permit limit of .0011 mg/l daily max was previously established for copper based on water quality standards and will be maintained in the draft permit. It is proposed that this limit be applied to the 30 day average as well.
candidates.computation_change_reason: The maintained 0.0011 mg/l value and its proposed application to 30-day averages determine which copper limit applies and whether daily or average results are compared for compliance.

candidates.exact_span: Because data is limited and discharge is infrequent, dissolved copper monitoring requirements will be maintained inthe draft permit.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether dissolved copper monitoring remains required despite infrequent discharge affects whether monitoring obligations were applicable during the evaluation period.

candidates.exact_span: The permittee reported a non-detect result for Cadmium, however the testing submitted by the permittee did not satisfy SSM.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether a non-detect that fails SSM counts as adequate evidence versus a documented no-data or insufficient-evidence state changes how missing cadmium results are classified.

candidates.exact_span: As previously described the permittee has not discharged in over five years and is unable to obtain a sample to analyze at the appropriate detection level.
candidates.computation_change_reason: A prolonged no-discharge period and inability to obtain an appropriately sensitive sample bear on whether cadmium monitoring was required and whether missing results reflect documented no-discharge, conditional non-requirement, or inadequate evidence.

candidates.exact_span: As a result, the detection limit used by the permittee .002 mg/l was used as the effluent concentration value in RP analysis.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Treating the reported detection limit as the effluent concentration for RP analysis affects whether numeric cadmium limits would have been derived and thus whether any enforceable limit applies.

candidates.exact_span: Because data is limited and based on presumptive values, Cadmium monitoring and reporting requirements will be added to the draft permit to obtain more current data for later RP analysis. Limits will not be prescribed.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Prescribing cadmium monitoring without numeric limits means cadmium may be report-only for limit comparison while still imposing monitoring obligations, changing both applicable-limit and monitoring-applicability outcomes.

candidates.exact_span: EPA proposes to continue to maintain the oil and grease narrative “no visible sheen” limitation.
candidates.computation_change_reason: A narrative sheen standard is not an ordinary numeric effluent limit, so different interpretation of its enforceability changes whether numeric compliance comparison is applicable for oil and grease.
